sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: In 2005, a young space engineer called Craig Clark moved back to his home city of Glasgow.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: He'd graduated from university just over a decade before, but the only jobs he could find were south of the border.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Now Craig wanted to start a company of his own.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: He called it Clyde Space.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: I went to school not far from the River Clyde, where the city's shipbuilding heritage was forged, and knew Glasgow had once been an industrial powerhouse.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: When I was a child, "Clyde-built" really meant something: craftsmanship and engineering excellence.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: There was a saying that I grew up with: "The Clyde made Glasgow and Glasgow made the Clyde." What I hadn't realised until recently was that, in a different guise, that tradition is still alive.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Two decades later, Glasgow is a European leader in building small satellites.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Many of those built here are known as CubeSats.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Their basic building block measures just 10cm by 10cm by 10cm - think of something about the size of a Rubik's Cube.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: They are much smaller, cheaper and quicker to develop than the huge contraptions that you might picture when you think of satellites.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: CubeSats - like this one, pictured in the offices of Spire Global in Glasgow - can be used for anything from weather forecasting to global positioning But crucially, they are modular and can be stacked together, then packed with cameras, sensors, communications equipment or other technology depending on their purpose.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: And their size belies their significance.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: The data collected by satellites of all kinds is increasingly woven into everyday life.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: It helps us communicate and navigate, track ships and transport goods, monitor forests and crops, manage energy networks and understand changes to our climate.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: For governments, that information can help inform decisions and respond to emergencies.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: As satellites have become more capable, space has become increasingly important.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: More than two decades after the first satellite company was established there, the Scottish Government says more small satellites are built in Glasgow than anywhere else in Europe.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Across Scotland, the wider space industry generated £335m in income in 2022-23 - up 69% in five years.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Excluding traditional satellite television broadcasting, it employed 2,811 people, an increase of 81% over the same period.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: But elsewhere in Europe, governments are committing big money to their own satellite industries.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Could this take investment and jobs away from Glasgow?
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: And if so, what - if anything - should the Scottish and UK governments do about it?
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: And what should be the role of the state when it comes to backing important industries?
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Perhaps the most surprising thing about Glasgow's success in the space industry is that it wasn't planned.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: One of the catalysts was Craig Clark's Clyde Space.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: The company specialised in CubeSats at just the right moment, a few years after it launched, as smaller and cheaper spacecraft were taking off, and would go on to build Scotland's first satellite, the UKube-1.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Crucially, the tech was built in partnership with the University of Strathclyde - which provided skills and research, as well as a ready supply of engineers.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Other companies followed, including Craft Prospect and Alba Orbital.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Expertise grew and a new space cluster began to form.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: American satellite company Spire chose Glasgow for its European base in 2015.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Smaller businesses developed, while established engineering and technology firms became part of the supply chain.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Glasgow has transformed itself into Europe's largest producer of small satellites - but some of the sector's leading figures say Glasgow's position is no longer secure.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Listen now on BBC Sounds.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Soon Glasgow was host to an "entire small satellite value chain", from components and satellite manufacturing, through to launch, spaceports and ground stations, according to Daniel Smith, founder of space marketing firm AstroAgency and the Scottish Government's trade and investment envoy for space.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: There are wider benefits too.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: According to a review commissioned by Space Scotland, space manufacturing alone accounted for more than 1,000 Scottish jobs in 2022-23.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: The wider industry generated £202m for the Scottish economy.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: And as the industry grew, so did the pool of knowledge.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: There are now more than 100 people working across space-related activity at the University of Strathclyde, with the subject now one of the institution's strategic priorities, according to Prof Malcolm Macdonald, its chair of applied space technology.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: The university works directly with commercial space companies on research and tech development.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Macdonald recalls that when he graduated, there was basically no local space industry for him to join.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Now, "when our graduates leave the university, they will go and work in the local space sector because it is now here in Glasgow for them", he says.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: But what's significant, Macdonald says, is that Glasgow's satellite industry wasn't something the government set out to establish.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Instead, the process was "largely organic", says Smith.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: By any measure it's a success story.
sentences.article_title: Europe is pouring billions into space. Can Glasgow's satellite industry keep up?

sentences.text: Next week, we'll hit our 100,000th visitor, which is a pretty extraordinary statistic.

sentences.text: The vast number of visitors report having a very good experience." Asked if the museum team had asked the embroidery's home museum in Bayeux for advice on queue management and timings, Cullinan said they had.

sentences.article_title: Indian singer Anuv Jain on finding success without the Bollywood boost

sentences.article_title: Indian singer Anuv Jain on finding success without the Bollywood boost

sentences.text: At one point, Jain was only releasing one song a year Jain says he's "very selective" about the music he releases, only putting out one song a year until recently.
sentences.article_title: Indian singer Anuv Jain on finding success without the Bollywood boost

sentences.text: But he plans to change that - and insists he has new songs coming "very soon".
sentences.article_title: Indian singer Anuv Jain on finding success without the Bollywood boost

sentences.text: "It's not like it's gonna be just one release, let's see how it works out." The singer explains that seeing a project through is key - which might be why he limits what he puts out.
sentences.article_title: Indian singer Anuv Jain on finding success without the Bollywood boost

sentences.text: "There are no projects like right now for me that are half or that I haven't completed them yet.
sentences.article_title: Indian singer Anuv Jain on finding success without the Bollywood boost

sentences.article_title: Indian singer Anuv Jain on finding success without the Bollywood boost

sentences.article_title: Indian singer Anuv Jain on finding success without the Bollywood boost

sentences.text: The singer also plays the guitar and has become known for his songs about deep emotions and themes There have been high-profile collaborations between some of western music and Indian music's biggest names in recent years.

sentences.article_title: Indian singer Anuv Jain on finding success without the Bollywood boost

sentences.text: The four Pearson children died during the petrol bomb attack, and their mother died 20 months later.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Four children had been "petrified" by a series of attacks on their home before a petrol bomb attack killed them all, an inquest has heard.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, Lia, three, died at their home in Jackson Street in Walkden in Greater Manchester in December 2017.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Their mother Michelle, 37, was badly burned and died in August 2019.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court - scheduled to last eight weeks - heard that Michelle had told police she did not feel safe in the house, which had been covered in graffiti and had its windows smashed.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Zak Bolland and David Worrall were jailed for life in 2018 for the murder of the four children, and in 2021 also convicted of Michelle's murder.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Bolland was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 40 years and Worrall was sentenced to life with a minimum of 37 years in jail.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Two weeks before the fatal attack, Bolland smashed windows at the house with a hammer, leaving glass everywhere.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: In a statement read out to the inquest, relatives said Michelle was traumatised and the called police on five separate occasions.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Her son Kyle – who escaped the blaze – said in a statement to the inquest that "the police didn't do anything".
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Michelle Pearson and her four children were murdered after an arson attack at their home in Walkden Michelle suffered 68% burns to her body and "clung on to life" until she died on August 25, 2019, around 20 months after the attack.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Her mother, Sandra Lever, said in a statement to the inquest that her daughter had been desperate to move house.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: "Michelle was beyond distressed," she said.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: "The children were petrified of living in Jackson Street." Relatives of the family said they believed their deaths were "wholly preventable" and raised "missed opportunities" to protect them.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Lever said her daughter had visited her social landlord to say she was in danger but had been told she did not meet the criteria for emergency housing.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Her children were having nightmares and Brandon had told her he no longer wanted to live in the house.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: But Michelle felt "fobbed off", the hearing was told.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Elaine Williams, a neighbour, said in the weeks before the arson attack she saw Bolland smashing the windows of Pearson's house with a hammer.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Williams said: "She wanted to move from there.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: "She was fed up of all the trouble.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: "She was at her wits' end.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: She was worried." Timothy Brennand, senior coroner for Greater Manchester West, told the hearing: "This is not a trial.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: This is not an exercise in blame and shame." He said the inquest would seek to examine whether there was "any predictable threat to life" and "what could or should have been done that might have prevented these deaths".
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: The coroner said the inquest aimed to give the Pearson family a voice, but added that their concerns "coalesce into two words of rhetoric – 'What if?'" Brennand read the remarks of Justice Davis, who jailed the family's killers.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Brennand said the judge had determined a series of tit-for-tat attacks had taken place as part of a feud in the lead-up to the fatal firebombing, but what lay behind the dispute had never been made public.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: She suffered massive injuries in the blaze and remained in hospital for a long time.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: For some of that time, she did not know her children were dead.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Her mental health deteriorated after she was told.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: When she died in hospital, her family placed a crucifix in her hand, and a photo of her children.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: "We know she's back with her children and out of pain," the family statement said.
sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.article_title: Murdered children 'petrified' by attacks on home, inquest told

sentences.text: Kieran Hayler denies the charges and has suggested his ex-wife, Katie Price, had "launched a campaign" against him when their marriage ended Katie Price's ex-husband, who is accused of raping a 13-year-old girl, told her to "not tell anyone" and said he might "get in trouble for this", a court has heard.
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: Kieran Hayler, 39, is on trial at Lewes Crown Court accused of three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault of the teenager in West Sussex in 2016, all of which he denies.
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: Earlier, jurors were told that on the first alleged occasion, Hayler told the 13-year-old he really liked her and began speaking to her about having sex.
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: He told her it was a "special thing" and they should do it, before he raped her, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: The court was played the complainant's police interview in which she said Hayler told her how special and "important" the first time was.
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: She said: "He started crying and saying, 'Maybe I shouldn't take it away from you, it's so important'." The complainant said she did not have a "conversation" with Hayler afterwards, and recalled thinking "I was probably a bit young".
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: Hayler allegedly raped the girl again on two further occasions.
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: The second occasion, she said, was two or three weeks later.
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: On this occasion she said she remembered waking up to Hayler being there, and after, he acted like "like nothing had happened".
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: On the third alleged occasion, the court heard Hayler told her she should not tell anyone, and then sexually assaulted her.
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: She said he told her: "You can't talk about it, you can't tell anyone, I might get in trouble for this." It is alleged he grabbed her hand and put it down his trousers.
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: Hayler was first interviewed by police in January 2022 and denied any of the allegations took place and that anything sexual occurred.
sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.article_title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told

sentences.text: The UK's biggest broadband provider, BT, has agreed to buy rival operator TalkTalk to save the company from collapse .
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: The takeover would end of months of speculation over the future of TalkTalk and mean services for its millions of customers will continue as normal.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: BT boss Alison Kirkby said it provided "a safety net" for TalkTalk customers.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: The administrator, Alvarez & Marsal, said it also provided certainty for TalkTalk's 900 staff based in Salford, Greater Manchester.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: However, Virgin Media called it a "stitch-up" which allows BT to "tighten its grip" over the market.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: The government has given itself the power to have the final say on the deal, citing its importance to vital public services.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: TalkTalk has 1.5 million retail customers and one million wholesale customers across the UK.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: BT's Kirkby told the BBC's Today programme: "Two and a half million customers, including vulnerable households, and key emergency services might have lost their services if Talk Talk had failed, which it was on track to do.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: "So BT stepped in as we were the only viable option to take the business forward." Ernest Doku from comparison website Uswitch said the deal means "nothing changes today".
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: "Your broadband and landline carry on as normal, and there is nothing you need to do right now," he added.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: However, he said that BT should explain "quickly and plainly what this means for contracts, prices and service in the future, so nobody is left guessing".
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: The regulator, Ofcom, says broadband customers should have the right to leave a contract without an exit fee , external if a new owner puts the price up beyond what was in the contract.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: TalkTalk began as a challenger to BT in the broadband market.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: It was listed on the London Stock Exchange, but was taken over by private equity in 2021.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: Since then, the firm has built up debt while losing customers, leaving it unable to pay some of those it owes money to.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: Despite this, TalkTalk remained the fourth biggest broadband provider in the UK, with 6.6% of customers, during the March to June period of this year, according to figures from analytic firm Opensignal.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: BT has 32.5% of customers, Sky 19.9%, and Virgin Media 19.1%.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: Rivals who were beaten to the deal by BT have said it will be bad for consumers.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: Tom O'Hagan, a former TalkTalk executive who was leading a takeover bid for the firm, told the BBC he was worried about "reduced choice and potentially an increase in price for consumers and for businesses" because of the BT deal.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: He added that he was particularly concerned about competition in the wholesale market, where TalkTalk's subsidiary PXC was BT's main rival.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: Virgin Media, which has also reportedly tried to buy TalkTalk in the past, said the BT takeover has "all the characteristics of a stitch-up masked as a rescue deal in the public interest".
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: It added that the purchase means BT can "roll its tanks over competition and further tighten its grip on the market.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: The logic simply doesn't add up." The Competition Markets Authority (CMA) will need to approve the takeover, which would give BT greater power over the broadband market.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: Tom Smith, a competition lawyer and former legal director at the CMA, said the regulator will be balancing that concern with other considerations.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: "When the CMA looks at it, it will look at what would have happened if the deal wasn't going through," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: DCMS has given the CMA until 19 October to deliver its verdict.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said: "Phone and broadband services are vital national infrastructure.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: "If TalkTalk services fail, there is a genuine risk to life and public services – including to hospitals, schools and emergency care.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: These are unprecedented circumstances that require action now." BT has said it welcomed the intervention and would "work constructively with the government and the CMA during their review".
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: Judith Mackenzie, a partner at investment manager Downing, told the BBC that broadband was "not a regulated industry, unlike electricity and water, but it's also very important to business users and ourselves, consumers".
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: "It's almost like a commodity now, broadband," she added.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: BT has said it will cost the firm £400m to buy TalkTalk out of administration.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: This includes the purchase price, fees, TalkTalk's expected £60m loss for this year, and BT effectively writing off the £100m TalkTalk owes BT's Openreach business.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: TalkTalk has £1.5bn of debt and made a £100m loss last year.
sentences.article_title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk

sentences.text: A mother on the school run sustained fatal injuries when a large pile of bricks fell on her head as she walked past a building site in east London, a court has heard.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: Michaela Boor, 29, was on Burdett Road in Bow on the morning of 27 March 2018 when the accident happened.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: She suffered a fractured skull and died two days later.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: Higgins Homes is on trial at the Old Bailey charged with corporate manslaughter and a health and safety offence.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: Four construction workers contracted by Higgins Homes - Thomas Anstis, Stephen Coulson, Dawood Maan and Alexander McInnes -  are accused of the same offences.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: Both the company and the four men deny the charges.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: Opening the case on Monday, prosecutor Alexandra Healy KC said Boor had been walking towards some shops with a friend, Chelsea Mustafa, when the bricks fell from a crane.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: She said: "Their route took them past a construction site that was being developed by Higgins Homes plc.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: "A pallet of bricks that was being transported by a tower crane towards a loading bay immediately adjacent to the pavement along Burdett Way fell on to them." The court heard the pallet caught on scaffolding while it was being hoisted, causing the bricks to fall.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: The prosecution claimed crane operator McInnes had a restricted view of the load and that the operation became a "blind lift" when it moved completely out of sight.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: Healy added: "Chelsea Mustafa ran into the road, away from the construction site.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: Although some bricks hit her on the back and her hand, she was able to avoid the bulk of the falling load.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: "Michaela Boor did not make it off the pavement.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: "She was hit by the falling bricks which fractured her skull and she sustained catastrophic brain injuries." Boor received treatment at the scene and was taken to the Royal London Hospital, but her injuries were "unsurvivable" and she died on 29 March, jurors were told.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: The bricks fell from a crane at a building site in east London in March 2018 Higgins Homes was the principal contractor and designer of the project to build a block of flats.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: The prosecution alleges there had been no risk assessment for lifting pallets of bricks so close to members of the public, and claimed Higgins Homes had not considered the safety of people outside the site.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: "Higgins Homes failed to give proper consideration to the protection of the public," Healy told the court.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: Anstis, 69, of Banstead, Surrey, was the senior site manager and temporary work co-ordinator.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: He was in charge of the building site and overseeing the work of subcontractors.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: The prosecutor claimed there was evidence showing that he "cut corners" to "save cost".
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: Coulson, 69, of Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire, was director of Coulson Lifting Services and was in charge of lifting services.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: He was not at the site on the day of the incident.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: Maan, 61, of Ashford, Kent, was the crane supervisor responsible for overseeing and supervising lifting operations on the site.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: McInnes, 34, of Islington, north London, was the crane operator.
sentences.article_title: Mother killed by falling bricks, court told

sentences.text: The UK Home Office has recorded 19,451 people crossing the Channel in small boats this year (file photo) Two men have died after trying to cross the English Channel off the coast of Berck in northern France.
sentences.article_title: Two men die in Channel crossing attempt off northern France

sentences.text: According to local media, police saw migrants leaving the beach on a boat at about 22:00 local time on Sunday, and when rescuers arrived, they were bailing water out of the overloaded vessel with their shoes.
sentences.article_title: Two men die in Channel crossing attempt off northern France

sentences.text: "When we arrived, there were at least 80 people on board and a terrible smell of gasoline,"Jean-Marc Lamblin, director of the French national sea rescue service (SNSM) told La Voix du Nord newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Two men die in Channel crossing attempt off northern France

sentences.text: Two women were taken to hospital after suffering burns that were caused by the mixture of gasoline in the seawater.
sentences.article_title: Two men die in Channel crossing attempt off northern France

sentences.text: Their condition has been described as not life-threatening.
sentences.article_title: Two men die in Channel crossing attempt off northern France

sentences.text: Lamblin told the newspaper that there were so many people on the boat, including children, that about 20 people were left stranded in the water because they could not get on board.
sentences.article_title: Two men die in Channel crossing attempt off northern France

sentences.text: He explained that when SNSM arrived, the two men, aged in their 30s and 40s, were in cardiac arrest.
sentences.article_title: Two men die in Channel crossing attempt off northern France

sentences.text: The men and injured women were brought back to shore where firefighters and paramedics helped them, but the men died at about midnight.

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "Our approach is to pick small goals we aim to prove with flight data and we construct an airframe for that one task." The X-plane philosophy is to "minimise goals, the more goals you have the more expensive it gets." For the X-59 it's about suppressing sonic booms on a budget and nothing else.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "We want to figure out what level of boom is acceptable to people on a regular basis," says Coen, who reckons his machine will sound "like a car door being closed across the street" when it flies past Mach 1, around 660mph at airline cruising altitude.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "It's likely that future X-planes will be uncrewed," says Coen, before adding the vital caveats "unless the technology we're researching relates to piloting or if crewing it is more cost-effective".

sentences.text: Europe's heatwave has boosted demand for battery storage systems As heatwaves scorched Europe this summer, workers at a US battery company noticed an uptick in demand.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: San Diego-based Unigrid sells a nine kilowatt hour battery for people's homes.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sweltering European homeowners were apparently looking for ways of storing power when it was available from the grid at lower rates.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They could then run air conditioners more cheaply, off the battery, during the worst heat of the day.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We have requests coming from Spain, France, Germany, The Netherlands," says Darren Tan, co-founder and chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've shipped the first 100 units and [expect to ship] 1,000 before the end of the year." Unigrid's battery is an emerging technology – it's a sodium ion, rather than lithium ion device.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries have got energy storage experts excited because they could end up much cheaper to build and operate than lithium ion.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They're potentially less likely to catch fire and should also work in a wider range of temperatures, even down to lows of minus 40C , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Darren Tan founded Unigrid - a maker of sodium ion batteries But there's a debate over what constitutes the best, and safest, sodium ion battery design.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Plus, more than one , external US company working in this space has floundered in recent years , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: China leads the world in sodium ion battery manufacturing at present so US competitors are going to have to work hard to keep up.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The prize that awaits is the possibility of batteries made in the US with 100% US-sourced materials.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is unlike lithium ion batteries, where China dominates the materials , external supply chain as well as manufacturing.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: For Tan, China has helped his company get to market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The Unigrid battery currently uses sodium ion cells made there, rather than in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We can switch back and forth and choose what battery we want to work with," says Tan, explaining that, in future, his firm might source cells from the US – though these may come at a different cost.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: There's another consideration.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Unigrid's battery contains chromium-3 in its cathode.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In a battery, electrons flow from cathode to anode , external when charging and in the opposite direction when discharging or providing power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Ivana Hasa, at the Warwick Manufacturing Group, University of Warwick, who has no connection to Unigrid, agrees that it is possible for chromium-3 to form chromium-6 at very high states of charge, though she says this can be mitigated by how voltage is controlled within the battery.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "Safety tests reported on the cell chemistry are very promising," she says of Unigrid's tech.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Tan says concerns around toxicity of the battery's materials are "overblown" and emphasises that Unigrid's battery has passed certification and safety tests for sale in Europe and is currently undergoing such evaluations for the US market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Third-party tests have not been able to get the battery to form chromium-6, he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've tried very hard to try and produce it, we've overcharged it as much as we can...
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: We were unsuccessful in generating chromium-6." The choice of cathode material, or how the electrolyte – which separates cathode and anode – is formulated are key details influencing the performance and longevity of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some manufacturers are not using chromium for their cathode but hard carbon instead, or sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (NFPP).
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In general, confidence around sodium ion batteries' reliability has increased during the last few years, says Prof Dame Grey, meaning they are now finding their way into grid storage applications.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Last December, LFP batteries – a relatively cheap form of lithium ion battery – were trading at $81 per kilowatt hour , external (kWh) whereas Unigrid's sodium ion battery pricing is roughly $100 kWh , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some companies that spoke to the BBC suggested sodium ion might reach as low as $30 per kWh but analysts say significantly lower costs could be many years away , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries are also not as energy dense as lithium ion batteries, meaning they must be slightly bigger and heavier in order to provide the same amount of power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The technology has been improving , external on this front in recent years but, even so, you're not likely to see sodium ion cells in small, energy hungry devices such as smartphones.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Larger energy storage solutions are where most people expect sodium ion to dominate.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Overcoming social anxiety can be tricky but experts have shared some tips to try and make it easier It was during her teenage years that Mary began to become anxious in social situations.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It got so bad she developed depression and had to have time off school.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: By the time she started university, she avoided group settings altogether.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I didn't join clubs and societies like others did," says Mary (not her real name).
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I just thought nobody would want to get to know me.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I didn't really make a single friend during my whole degree." Mary's social anxiety was so bad that she was diagnosed as having social anxiety disorder - something that affects up to 12% of people , external at some point in their lives.

sentences.text: But plenty more report struggling more generally.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Research has suggested more than a fifth of university students face some kind of social anxiety during their studies – and it has been linked to lower grades, poorer relationships and isolation in a study by the universities of Chichester, Coventry and University College London , external .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "When I first got there I went to one society, but everybody was talking to each other and I had a sudden fear come over me.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I felt I wouldn't fit in and I went home." Mary, who is now 25, describes her social anxiety as like an out of body experience.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: When she was talking to new people, heat would rise in her face and her hands would begin to tingle.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I'd almost feel myself separating from my body.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I forgot how to form words," she says.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "After social situations I was often left with the sense that I'd done something awful.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I had an all-consuming feel of shame.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I kept thinking there was something fundamentally flawed in me." Neil Greening, chair of the Social Anxiety Alliance UK, says this is a typical characteristic of people with social anxiety.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People think they have a personality flaw.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: They internalise it rather than seeing it as a recognisable condition that they can get help for." The key thing to remember: It's fairly normal to feel a little shy or anxious when meeting new people, being in new situations or going for a job interview.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Social anxiety is when it actually stops people doing things, Greening says.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: For those with a clinical diagnosis it can have a debilitating impact like it did for Mary.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "It can be hard to admit to any form of social anxiety in a world where extrovertism and social confidence is generally admired.

sentences.text: Mary, who has moved on to do a postgraduate course, is now managing her social anxiety better.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: After her undergraduate degree she got support from the NHS in the form of a talking therapy called CBT.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It is considered the gold standard treatment for social anxiety and encourages people to re-frame their thoughts and change their behaviours.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Prof David Clark, a psychologist at the University of Oxford, says he would like to see more people come forward for therapy but says people can also take steps to help themselves.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: The first step, he says, is to stop obsessive self-focus .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People with social anxiety often monitor themselves constantly during social situations.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "Focus outwardly on the conversation, other person or your surroundings." He says you also need to test your fears with behavioural experiments by asking a question in a meeting or saying something in a group and noticing what happens.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People with social anxiety often assume negative outcomes – that they will embarrass themselves or think others will find them boring.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Testing that can help people break that.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It's frightening, but it can really help." He also says they need to drop safety behaviours , such as rehearsing every sentence, avoiding eye contact or sticking close to one particular person.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: And finally, Clark adds, try to avoid post-event rumination .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "It's so easy to distort what actually happened." This is something Mary can empathise with.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I used to play things over constantly in my mind.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: What I've learnt is that dealing with social anxiety is a gradual process.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: The therapy really helped me, but so did something a friend said to me a couple of years ago.

sentences.text: "When I said I didn't want to join her in meeting some of her friends, citing my poor social skills, she said she'd never thought that about me and that I shouldn't undersell myself.

sentences.text: I was overcome with emotion.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Mark and Roberta Harrison say Hobie was funny and mischievous The police watchdog has criticised a force after call handlers told a family raising mental health concerns to ring a locksmith.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: On 6 August 2025, Hobie Harrison's parents called Norfolk Police to request a welfare check after he failed to respond to them.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: He was found dead the next day.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said the force's 101 call handlers should have referred the family to mental health services, but instead suggested they contacted a locksmith.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Norfolk Police said it was reviewing the findings and it had been following the force's Right Care, Right Person (RCRP) policy , external , which limits officer attendance at welfare calls to cases involving "immediate risk to life".
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The IOPC said the call handlers should have asked more probing questions to assess Hobie's level of risk and there should have been a better explanation to his parents about why officers were not sent under its RCRP guidelines.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Hobie's parents, Mark and Roberta Harrison, made a second request for a welfare check for their son to Norfolk Police the following day.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Officers attended and found the 30-year-old dead in his flat in Norwich.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The couple say they were left unsure where to turn after being told their concerns for their son did not meet the threshold for a police response In October 2025, the family made a complaint to Norfolk Police over its handling of their call.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: In its report, the IOPC criticised Norfolk Police's response to that complaint after the force told the parents officers should not have attended either call, including the second one that led to Hobie's body being found.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The IOPC called that reply "unnecessary and insensitive".
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Hobie had previously threatened suicide and Mark said: "We'll never know whether he was still alive when we first called and whether something could have been done.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: David Ford, the watchdog's director of oversight and casework, said: "We have raised our concerns with the force around its interpretation of RCRP and monitoring of the initiative.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "As a result... the force has said it will undertake a review to examine whether there are any organisational learnings." Norfolk Police said it could not comment further because an inquest has yet to take place, which is due to happen in November.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Hobie's parents say the 30-year-old loved music and enjoyed gardening Hobie had schizophrenia and developmental trauma and was under the care of the Norfolk and Suffolk Foundation Trust Community Mental Health Team.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: His parents said he had a history of drug use.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The couple adopted Hobie as a child and said he had been in "good spirits" the last time they saw him before his death.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: In August 2025, the family said they became concerned he had not spoken to them for more than 24 hours as he usually contacted them "several times a day".
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "The non-contact was just... it didn't happen.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: So, it was very, very unusual," said Roberta.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The couple went to Hobie's flat but could not use their key to get inside because his key was still in the lock on the inside of the door.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "We were 100% certain he was in there and he wasn't responding, so we knew there was something seriously wrong," said Mark.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: If you have been affected by any of the issues in this story, you can visit the BBC Action Line for support and information Unable to break in, they called Norfolk Police and told call handlers that their son had a history of self-harm and suicidal threats.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: After consulting a supervisor, the staff member told them the situation did not meet the threshold for a police response and suggested they consider contacting a locksmith.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "We didn't know how to make a decision at that point or what to do quite frankly," said Roberta.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The following morning, after a second call to police, officers attended the flat and found Hobie's body.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "If the police are no longer going to come, then it has to be very clear who's got the responsibility," Roberta added.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The Harrisons say regular calls, walks, shopping trips and meals together formed part of their daily routine with Hobie RCRP was first developed by Humberside Police in 2019 and has since been adopted by forces across England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The policy is intended to reduce police involvement in welfare and mental health-related incidents so officers can focus on crime and immediate threats to life.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Norfolk Police said the approach, which it introduced in 2024, had reduced officer attendance at welfare-related incidents, from 11,831 in the year before the policy was introduced to 9,229 by its second year.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The force said there was "no defined response" to welfare concerns and the appropriate pathway depended on the circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: His family say Hobie enjoyed riding his bike when he felt well enough to get out and about The Norfolk and Suffolk Integrated Care Board said support could involve health, social care, ambulance or police services.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: A 2024 national agreement on the policy , external said people experiencing mental health crises should not be left without support.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Some coroners have raised concerns about RCRP.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: A Prevention of Future Deaths  report into the death of Sophie Cotton in County Durham , external said the policy appeared to overlook that mental health teams could not enter locked premises.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Reports into the deaths of Paul Alexander in West Yorkshire , external and Andrew Hughes in Manchester , external also highlighted gaps in RCRP response arrangements.

sentences.text: A new NHS-style social care system for England could take decades to be implemented, economist Sir Andrew Dilnot has told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: Sir Andrew, who led a commission proposing reform of the system 15 years ago, said Prime Minister Andy Burnham appeared to want social care to be completely free, including residential costs.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme the cost of such a scheme would be "very substantial".
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: And with Burnham promising to put his plans before voters at the next general election, Sir Andrew said change "is now further away".
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: Adult social care provides state support to help people live more independently, including assistance at home.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: However, unlike the NHS, social care is not free at the point of use in England, leaving some people facing huge bills.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: In an interview with the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg , Burnham suggested his proposals for social care would mean "everyone contributes, everyone is covered" and refused to rule out tax rises to fund such a system.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: He promised to set out more details of his vision in his conference speech on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: However, he suggested any proposals would not be implemented before the next general election, as he wanted to stick to the commitments in Labour's 2024 election manifesto, which included a promise not to increase national insurance, income tax or VAT.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: Labour MP and former minister Darren Jones told Laura Kuenssberg that scrapping the pensions triple lock was an "option that the government should consider alongside others" in order to fund social care reforms.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: The triple lock pension policy guarantees that the state pension will increase by either average wage growth, inflation or 2.5% - whichever is highest - and keeping it in place is also a Labour manifesto pledge.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: But Helen Miller, director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies think tank, said scrapping the triple lock would not be enough to pay for social care and tax rises would also probably be needed.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: The next general election is not due until August 2029, although Burnham could choose to call one earlier.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: Sir Andrew told the BBC change on social care "is now further away" than had been implied when Burnham first promised a new national care service for England in a speech in July, shortly after he became prime minister.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: He pointed out that if proposals are included in Labour's 2029 election manifesto, that would be 30 years after Sir Tony Blair launched a royal commission on social care and more than 15 years since his own commission reported back.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: Social care reform could mean big risks and big rewards for Burnham Why the PM could finally drop the triple lock pension pledge By promising an NHS-style system for social care, Sir Andrew said the PM was implying it would be "entirely free".
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: In England and Northern Ireland, people with assets worth more than £23,250 - including their home - are not currently entitled to help with care costs from their council.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: In Wales, social care is also means-tested.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: In Scotland, state-funded personal care is offered to all adults who are assessed as needing help with tasks including eating and bathing.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: However, this does not include accommodation, food and everyday living costs, which are subject to means testing.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: Sir Andrew said a Scottish-style system would still leave people in residential care facing "very substantial bills", which Burnham has said he wants to avoid.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: The Health Foundation has estimated a universal social care system in England, with the government funding all support, could cost around £18.5bn a year.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: On Sunday, Burnham said he believed the costs would be lower than this but he has not set out how he would fund his plans.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: Sir Andrew said he believed an NHS-style social care system could costs "well in excess of £18bn", although a Scottish model could cost half this figure.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: He added that a system where the amount people must pay towards their care is capped, "could still work well for elderly people".
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: Sir Andrew's own commission proposed a lifetime cap of £35,000.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: The report's recommendations were accepted by the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government, led by David Cameron.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: However, the implementation of the cap was delayed to 2020, with Cameron blaming pressure on the public finances, and the idea was eventually dropped by subsequent Conservative governments.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: Other proposals to reform the system have also failed, with Theresa May's Conservative government scrapping plans to make people receiving care at home pay the full costs if they were worth at least £100,000, after this was branded a "dementia tax" by opponents.
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: Meanwhile, when he was health secretary in Gordon Brown's government, Burnham's plan for a national care service suggested this could be paid for through a compulsory contribution from people's estates after they die.

sentences.text: The idea was branded a "death tax" by Labour's opponents and the proposals went no further after the party lost the 2010 general election.

sentences.text: NHS staff in England suspected of looking at patient records without a valid reason will be immediately suspended as part of a "zero-tolerance crackdown" on snooping.
sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records

sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records

sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records

sentences.text: The move follows a series of high-profile incidents involving the records of Nottingham and Southport attack victims and a child who was injured in a crocodile enclosure in Cambridgeshire .
sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records

sentences.text: This week, Bristol Foundation NHS Trust said it had launched an internal investigation after it emerged the medical records of an 18-year-old had been accessed years after his death .
sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records

sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records

sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records

sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records

sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records

sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records

sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records

sentences.article_title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records
