sentences.text: Dr Chris McCarthy says the pillow that's best for you depends on the way you sleep (branding has been obscured) "I am one of those people," says Dr Chris McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "I do take my pillow with me." You may have seen those people at the airport - a pillow stuffed under an arm as they drag their suitcases to check-in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Or you might be one yourself - attached to a pillow that's soft enough to settle into but robust enough that it's not bunched into a ball by morning.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy insists he's not being fussy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He's a top physiotherapist and knows the wrong pillow can be a pain in the neck.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He doesn't take his abroad, but as soon as he gets to his hotel he starts "faffing about" with the pillows - and he's got a tried and tested trick to make even the most lacklustre one fit for sleep.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Here's his guide to choosing the perfect pillow for you.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: What makes the perfect pillow?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: One advertised for your sleeping position?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Sliced Bread separates science fact from the marketing fiction.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy, an associate professor at the Manchester School of Physiotherapy, says the right pillow will depend on what position you sleep in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He tells the BBC's Sliced Bread podcast that most people fall into one of three categories of sleeper: side, back or front.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy discourages front sleeping as your neck is turned one way for a long period of time.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Inevitably a muscle or ligament gets stretched and a bit irritated," he says.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If there's one thing there's a really good consensus on... in the physiotherapy world about treating spinal pain, it's don't sleep on your front." When choosing a pillow, back sleepers should consider the flexion at the top of their spine, a curving that increases naturally in many people as they age.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If you have a bigger bend "it means you need a slightly thicker pillow than someone who's got a very flat back," says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For side sleepers the key measurement is the width of your shoulders.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: In general, the broader you are the thicker the pillow you will need.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But you also need to consider your mattress.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy says how much you sink into your mattress "makes a huge difference in the subsequent height you then need from the pillow".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Broad shoulders need a thick pillow [if] you're on a very firm mattress," he explains.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If you're on a softer mattress, then you need a thinner pillow because your shoulder sinks into the mattress [more]." This is less of an issue for back sleepers as they don't sink into the mattress as much as side sleepers do.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If your pillow feels too flat, McCarthy suggests placing a folded towel underneath and changing the number of folds to adjust the height.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Then you can make a rough measurement to help you pick a new one.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Specialist pillows are often advertised as contoured, ergonomic or orthopaedic - but McCarthy says their effectiveness isn't completely proven.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "There is a little bit of fairly scrappy evidence to suggest that having a little bit of a higher front of the pillow, which goes into the neck area... does help [side sleepers]." To see if a higher front helps you sleep better, you can try McCarthy's towel trick by rolling it and placing it underneath your pillow.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He urges side sleepers to pick a position that keeps their back straight.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For back sleepers, some manufacturers advertise a pillow with a dip in the middle that is raised at the sides.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: It does put people into a good sleeping position, says McCarthy, but some of his patients have found them "a bit claustrophobic".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Someone who has a large and heavy head also needs a thicker and firmer pillow, he adds.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Feather and down can keep you cool on warm nights because they wick away heat from your head, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But they can change shape during the night, particularly if the sleeper moves around a lot and the pillow can end up bunched towards the headboard.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "What starts off as a nice, flat, supported surface becomes a wedge and so your neck is then kinked up." Hollow fibre and microfibre fillings can hold shape better though they generally don't wick away heat as well, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Some are made with a firmer material in the lower half of the pillow, which help retain the shape during the night.

sentences.text: York was the subject of the city-wide pilot, which also put on workshops for parents and offered special training for early years staff.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Twenty local authorities across England are now signed up to launch similar schemes to tackle the number of pupils starting school without being fully toilet-trained.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The government said the pilot's results were "encouraging", and confirmed they were committed to 75% of pupils reaching a good level of development at the end of their first year in school by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Since April this year, parents across York have been targeted via GP surgeries, pharmacies, family hubs, schools, nurseries and libraries with information and offers of support on how to potty-train their child ahead of starting school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Potty training guides were sent out to all families across York who had a child starting reception in September - with the aim that all children could use the toilet independently by the time they started school, except those with medical issues or special educational needs.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The results from all 55 mainstream primary schools across the city, shared exclusively with BBC News, suggested there had been a 43% drop since last year in the number of children who were not fully toilet-trained when they started school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Across York last September, 148 out of 1,364 reception pupils (11%) were recorded as not being toilet-trained when they started school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: This year, that fell to 85 reception pupils out of 1,374 (6%).
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Parents Natalie and Lucy, who both have daughters starting reception next year, have welcomed the extra support on offer.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Mum Natalie says there's a lot of conflicting pressures on parents about the right time to potty-train Lucy said she had noticed the drop-in sessions on potty training in her local children's centre and thought it was a "really good idea".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "I think it's really important that children are more prepared for that aspect of starting school," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Natalie said getting her daughter Freya potty-trained in time for school has been a priority, but feels there is a lot of pressure on parents to do so.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "I think going to school is hard enough for children," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When I was little, we still had the terry towelling nappies and they had to be washed and hung on the line.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So I think with disposable nappies it's easier," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Around one in four children started school in England and Wales last year not fully toilet-trained, and teachers said they have been spending over an hour a day changing nappies, according to the latest research from the children's charity Kindred Squared , external .
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Felicity Gillespie, chief executive of Kindred Squared, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that children not being potty trained when starting school was "a real concern for teachers".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "They tell us that they're losing, on average across the country, a day a week of teaching time to dealing with potty-training issues." Gillespie is keen to spread the message that "it's best for children to be coming out of nappies" when they are between 18 and 30 months old.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When the teacher's leaving the class to change someone's nappy, the rest of the class is having their learning broken up.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So everybody loses out,” she added.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The ability to listen to and follow instructions is another skill that helps pupils get the most out of learning when they start reception class Jo Mould, who teaches reception at Robert Wilkinson Primary Academy in York, said she has noticed an improvement in pupils being ready for school this year.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "We've spent more time teaching in these last three weeks than we have in previous years," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "The children have come in so ready to learn, because they're more settled and regulated socially and emotionally.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: We've had a really, really positive start to the school year." Jo Mould says not having to deal with toilet training has meant more time spent teaching her pupils York councillor Bob Webb said the impact of the scheme had been "so positive" for both schools and families.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: But he acknowledged a potential "gap in support" for parents between seeing health visitors with their toddler, and the child later arriving at school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".

sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.

sentences.text: England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said the change to inspections, rolled out nationally just under a year ago, had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted said it had worked closely with unions and parents to develop the new report card inspection system and that it would continue to grade schools.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted, England's schools inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry , who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An example of a new Ofsted inspection report But the new system has faced criticism since it was first proposed , with Perry's sister Prof Julia Waters saying it appeared to be "a rehash of the discredited and dangerous system it is meant to replace".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT issued a claim in the High Court for a judicial review over the changes, arguing there had not been adequate consultation on the new report cards before they were introduced, but this was rejected.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Nearly a year after it was fully rolled out, the NAHT said evidence from its members suggested the new system is having a detrimental impact on school leaders' mental health.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Testimonies seen by the BBC suggest head teachers are being left "overwhelmed" and "anxious", with the pressure caused by the inspections described as "intolerable".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Although the system had been changed with the intention of lowering the burden on school leaders, the testimonies say the inspection and assessment process had become "higher stakes than ever before".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Amanda Hulme, head teacher at Claypool Primary School in Bolton, said a recent inspection at her school had been "easily the most stressful experience" of her career.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I'll continue the work that I do with head teachers, head teacher representatives and others to make sure that we get this Ofsted framework, but also the culture and the whole regime, right," she said.

sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The largest teaching union had objected to the prospect of partly funding a 3.5% pay increase this year out of existing school budgets Schools in England are to get around £500 million in extra funding towards the teachers' pay award this school year, reducing the risk of a strike ballot by the largest education union.

sentences.text: Schools had been expected to fund some of the 3.5% teachers pay increase for the current school year out of their existing budgets, which National Education Union (NEU) leaders had strongly objected to.

sentences.text: Daniel Kebede, the general secretary of the NEU, said the offer of more funding was a "significant" step in negotiations.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: In a letter to the union on Wednesday, which has been seen by the BBC, the government said the increase would be funded by savings in employers' contributions to the local government pension scheme.

sentences.text: The letter said the 4.9 percentage point drop in what employers are expected to contribute will deliver "significant savings" on the pay bill for support staff, which will not be clawed back by central government.

sentences.text: The National Education Union said it expected the extra money to be around £500m, which schools can now use towards teachers' pay this year.

sentences.text: In July, ministers accepted the recommendation of the independent pay review body for teachers and agreed a 3.5% increase from September 2026 would be followed by 3% the following year.

sentences.text: Luke Sibieta, IFS research fellow, said the extra money would mean the pay increase this year was fully funded - and on top of other funding increases, schools would be £1.6bn better off by next year than they had expected this summer.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The additional money could potentially bring the uplift for this year into line with next year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Kebede said schools has been "running on empty" and the funding signalled "a welcome return to reality, and a message of hope for the entire school community".

sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Similarly, the NASUWT union welcomed the news.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: General secretary Matt Wrack added schools needed "a sustainable, long-term injection of extra funding" to meet the needs of young people.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: When parenting advice becomes too much Before Rosie Whitfield became a mum, she imagined herself parenting very calm children.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Then I had two wild boys," she says with a laugh.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Following the birth of her kids, Rosie spent hours online looking for the best advice and was drawn to one particular approach to parenting: Gentle parenting, which focuses on empathy and mutual respect with little emphasis on punishment, albeit with boundaries.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But she constantly worried her choices, from sleep schedules to handling toddler tantrums, were "ruining their lives forever".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Rosie believes her confidence and intuition were stripped away as she questioned every parenting decision.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Government research suggests that around two-thirds of parents with young children feel overwhelmed by the amount of parenting information available and struggle with conflicting advice, with many turning to social media for support.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Rosie Whitfield says she felt overwhelmed by the amount of parenting advice online when looking for guidance on raising her two sons.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: And it's not just the early years.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Research from the charity Action for Children found that many parents of teenagers who initially contacted the charity for help with school avoidance, ADHD or mental health, often went on to describe their own anxiety, exhaustion and uncertainty of how to parent with empathy and patience when close to burnout.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Faced with an array of parenting philosophies, or "brands" to choose from, is all of this advice helping parents or making them more anxious?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: And is there really a best way to parent?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Or, as we strive to become the perfect parent, are we losing our intuition?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Parents today are confronted by parenting styles including "helicopter parenting", which is focused on closely monitoring and protecting children from harm, and "tiger parenting", which involves strict parenting and high expectations for achievement.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: There are also "snowplough parents", who try to remove obstacles from their child's path, and "dolphin parents", who aim to be firm but flexible.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Author Matilda Gosling, who wrote Evidence‑Based Parenting, says many of the parenting fads or trends complicate what should be a straightforward relationship between a parent and child.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Throughout history, you get these swings from one extreme to the other," she says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Gentle parenting is seen by some as the latest swing away from a strict, detached parenting style popular in the 1990s, which often relied on controlled crying, the naughty step and time out.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: It is built around understanding, empathy and respect but also emphasises the importance of boundaries.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: One of the most widely studied models of parenting comes from developmental psychologist Diana Baumrind.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Baumrind identified three parenting styles, later expanded to four: authoritative (high warmth and high control), authoritarian (low warmth and high control), permissive (high warmth and low control), and neglectful (low warmth and low control).
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Authoritative is the gold standard," says Gosling who has looked at more than 1,000 studies.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Research has found that children raised with an authoritative approach, combining warmth with clear boundaries, tend to achieve better academic results, have higher self-esteem and stronger social skills.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But where gentle parenting fits within that framework is disputed.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Gosling believes that it falls on the permissive side.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It's very much child-led.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: The child ends up having so much control that there's no sense of safety coming from the outside." However, Sarah Ockwell-Smith, who is widely credited with coining and popularising the term 'gentle parenting', strongly disagrees.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It [gentle parenting] is not remotely permissive," she says, putting it firmly in Baumrind's authoritative category.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Clear boundaries are "super important".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Social media, however, is flooded with memes of exhausted parents calmly negotiating with a child having a supermarket meltdown, something Ockwell-Smith finds deeply frustrating.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "I have to step away from the Instagram reels and the TikToks because I just want to comment, 'This is not gentle parenting'".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "You have house rules, family limits, discipline and consequences.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But the difference is we look at discipline as learning and teaching rather than punishing." Toddler tantrums and teenage behaviour, she argues, should be viewed through a lens of ongoing brain development, not 'they're being naughty' or 'they hate me'.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But despite the term being popular, Ockwell-Smith believes that gentle parenting is still a fringe movement and that authoritarian parenting remains the dominant style.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Around 80 years ago, American paediatrician Dr Benjamin Spock published a book called Baby and Child Care, which went on to sell millions of copies and became the main source of advice for mothers for generations.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: The opening line was "Trust yourself.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: You know more than you think..." The book challenged strict parenting norms of the time and in the following decades parents were offered more advice from an increasing range of voices.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Research into parenting has increasingly focused on the early years - from pregnancy to the age of two when the building blocks for lifelong emotional and physical health are laid down.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: For parents, that means more advice to navigate competing messages about what is best for their children.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Professor Ellie Lee, the director of the Centre for Parenting Culture Studies, has studied parenting for more than two decades, including research into mothers' confidence and uncertainty around infant feeding.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: She says a major shift occurred in the 1990s when parenting became an increasing focus of public policy.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Politicians started to say 'Parenting's the hardest job in the world.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Children don't come with a manual.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: We need to give parents guidance.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Parents need more support.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: We need parent education'." Advice began to emerge on almost every aspect of family life, from tummy time, to feeding, to the right buggy, she explains.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Prof Lee argues that while some public health campaigns were necessary, such as advice not to put babies to sleep on their front after research into cot deaths, the growing culture of advice began to make parents paranoid.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Dr Spock's 'trust yourself' philosophy is now a very counter-cultural piece of advice," she says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "What we say instead is 'always seek help'," Sarah Ockwell-Smith is widely credited with coining and popularising the term 'gentle parenting' She believes this has made parents more anxious about doing things "right".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Some of the things that are now presented as really high stakes are not," she says, using examples like breastfeeding exclusively for six months or how much tummy time a child needs.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It's terrible because parents become completely exhausted." Ockwell-Smith says the volume of advice can be "deafening and confusing".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Actually, parents should just learn themselves and go on intuition," she says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Others point out that there is also a problem of advice being given that is altogether wrong.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Ruth Watts is a health visitor who began sharing content on social media after becoming concerned about misinformation online.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: She had seen "experts" advise parents to wean babies onto solids early, offer treatment advice for tongue tie or allergies without medical training, and tell parents to put babies in their own rooms before six months.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Many families, she argues, are working longer hours while at the same time health services are being stripped back, leaving more parents looking online for breastfeeding, behaviour and sleep support.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "We are looking for that kind of personable, conversational approach from people, rather than reading a website." Many factors shaping family life remain outside parents' control.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: A child's temperament, special educational needs, family support, finances and their own upbringing can all influence family life.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: While some say parenting hasn't got harder but expectations have, others argue that parents today are facing more complex challenges than in previous generations with growing concerns around young people's mental health.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: There are also debates around children spending more time on screens and less time outdoors, while schools are reporting increasing behavioural challenges and lower respect for rules and authority.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Prof Lee believes parental confidence is at an all-time low.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "I think parents feel very nervous about disciplining children now because they're worried about how it's going to make them feel," she argues.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: The confusion around the "right" way to parent has led some parents to turn to courses for help.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Aymara Lamche-Brennan, who has a 22-year-old daughter, four-year-old son and six-month-old daughter, signed up for a course during the summer when another mother at the school gate mentioned she was attending.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Aymara Lamche-Brennan, pictured with her three children, signed up for a Circle of Security parenting course "The flyer said 'it's the toughest job in the world' and I thought yes it is, how can you help?'" Aymara says from her home in London.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It's not telling you how to parent.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: It's helping you think," says Jennifer Peters, a former social worker and director of the charity Connected Lives which runs courses across London, Derbyshire and Cambridgeshire.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: She says most parents want the best for their kids but they don't always know how to get there, and that guidance can be helpful.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "I don't think people need to be bombarded with information but the group experience helps you think, 'oh, it's not just me' and lets you take a step back from it all," Peters says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Back in Dubai, Rosie says the arrival of her second child changed everything as she realised her sons were "polar opposites" and there is no one-size-fits-all solution.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: A recent trip home to Birmingham also provided some perspective.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Her eldest son was throwing a tantrum, and Rosie found herself wrestling with a familiar worry.

sentences.text: "If I send him upstairs, am I damaging him emotionally?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Is he going to develop an attachment disorder because of this?" But her mum said, 'Just send him upstairs.

sentences.text: He can't hit his brother over the head with a horse [if he is upstairs].
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Follow through with your actions.' Rosie is taking this "generational advice" on board and has started "venting on social media" to show other mums that they are not alone.

sentences.text: For the first time in more than 30 years, a hurricane has not formed in the Atlantic throughout September - normally the most active month for hurricane activity.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: With just two months left of the defined hurricane season, there is an increasing possibility that no hurricanes will develop at all.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: This would make the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season the only one in the satellite era without a hurricane.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: The biggest reason for this is El Niño, which traditionally stifles activity in the Atlantic but brings a very active season in the eastern North Pacific.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: The Atlantic hurricane season was predicted to be quieter than normal as a result of this.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: With a very strong El Niño forecast, the US National Hurricane Center in May predicted a total of eight to 14 named storms.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: Of those, three to six were predicted to become hurricanes, with one to three becoming major hurricanes.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: September is typically the most active month for tropical storm and hurricane activity.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: But, this year marks the latest date on record since the start of the satellite era (1960s onward) where no hurricane has formed in the North Atlantic.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: While there have been no hurricanes forming in the North Atlantic so far this season, the Eastern North Pacific has been very active with above-average storms There were, however, four named tropical storms that formed in September: Edouard, Fay, Gonzalo and Hanna.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: All but Edouard stayed out in the open waters of the Atlantic.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: The National Hurricane Center suggests there is no sign of any tropical storm activity or hurricane over the next week at least.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: Forecasters at Colorado State University, who also monitor activity, suggest the strong El Niño is likely to disrupt wind patterns across the Atlantic and "likely result in below-normal activity" over the next two-weeks.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: As the typical peak of the season has passed and is now on a downward trend until 30 November, a season without a single hurricane is looking increasingly possible.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: As wind patterns shift during an El Niño, upper winds over the Atlantic increase and this leads to more wind shear, where wind changes rapidly with height.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: Strong winds blowing at different speeds and directions at higher altitudes rip apart thunderstorms, preventing them from growing into tropical storms or hurricanes.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Pacific typically becomes more active during El Niño because the sea surface temperatures here are much higher, combined with more favourable wind patterns.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: The warmer waters give storms more energy to grow into tropical storms and hurricanes.
sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.article_title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.

sentences.text: One of the best-known meteor showers is now active until 7 November.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: The Orionids are particularly fast and can leave trails in the sky that last a few seconds after the meteor itself has gone.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: The display occurs at around the same time each year when the Earth passes through a trail of dust and debris left behind by Halley's Comet.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: The showers peak overnight from 21 to 22 October.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: The Orionids are particularly fast, entering the atmosphere at around 41 miles per second.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: As tiny particles from Halley's comet enter the Earth's atmosphere they heat up and produce streaks of light across the night sky that we see as meteors.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: Halley's Comet is one of the most famous comets in our Solar System and has been observed from Earth for centuries.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: It takes around 76 years to complete one orbit of the Sun and was last seen from Earth in 1986.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: Halley's Comet is not expected to be visible from Earth again until 2061, but its debris will continue to produce meteor showers each year.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: In fact, the Earth encounters material left behind by it twice a year, resulting in the Eta Aquariid meteor shower in May and the Orionids in October.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: The meteors appear to radiate from the constellation of Orion, which is where the shower gets its name, but they can appear anywhere across the night sky.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: Under ideal conditions, around 10 to 20 meteors can be seen each hour at the shower's peak.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: The constellation of Orion is one of the most recognisable in the night sky identifiable by the large hour glass shape formed by some of its stars For the best chance of seeing them, find a dark location away from street lights and with as wide a view of the sky as possible.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: Allow around 15 to 20 minutes for your eyes to adjust.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: You won't need binoculars or a telescope; the shower is best viewed with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: Later in October, the Moon could affect how many meteors are visible at the peak of the Orionids, as as it builds to its full phase on 26 October.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: This means its light could make some of the fainter meteors more difficult to see.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: Brighter meteors, however, should still be visible, particularly from darker locations away from artificial light.
sentences.article_title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower

sentences.text: A team, from Queen's University Belfast (QUB), are heading to Florida later this month to take part in a Nasa 'lunabotics' competition.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Lunabotics is a university-level competition for teams to use the Nasa systems engineering process to design, build, and operate a lunar robot.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: The students created a lab-built robot that they will bring to the competition to find out how it would deal with future moon missions.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: The robots will be expected to dig up lunar material, drive over obstacles and use the material to form a wall.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Jack Fitzpatrick, who's studying for a PhD in mechanical engineering, said "it's a great feeling" to have been invited and they're looking forward to the opportunity to take part.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Jack Fitzpatrick is studying for a PhD and is part of the mechanical team The team of 10 QUB students made it to the competition following their win at the competition earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: They'll be competing at the University of Central Florida against university teams from Australia, India and the US.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Jamie Smith is the team's software lead Jamie Smith is a third-year electrical and electronic engineering student.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: He explained that the team was divided into three groups for software, electronics and mechanical.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Jamie was the software team lead for this project.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: He said their main task was to control the rover then provide the autonomous capabilities towards it.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: And, they had to build rover simulations to test their software before they actually got one.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Jack, however, is part of the mechanical side.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: "We analyse that something is physically strong enough, it's well built enough to survive this environment, it's going to have the traction to drive in this environment," he explained.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Jack Fitzpatrick, Sandro O'Hara, Eoin Conway, Jamie Smith and Alex Dunne Jamie explained they designed the 52 kg aluminium frame robot rover and took it compete at a competition in Milton Keynes.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: We ended up winning the competition and had great fun," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Then a few weeks later, they were invited to compete at Nasa's international Lunabotics competition.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Jack said that being asked to go was a "great feeling" and "a real opportunity to demonstrate everything that you've learned".
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: "It's just a great opportunity to represent Northern Ireland, the UK and really Europe abroad as we are the only European team that will be there," Jack explained.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Both of the students said their success was a reflection of both themselves and also the university and the School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Jamie explained that the main objective of the rover is that should be able to drive itself around a lunar-simulated room.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: "That means it should start at a point, figure out where it is within this room, travel to an excavation point, so in that point, it will pick up then some sand which is  meant to be lunar-simulant.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: "It'll pick up the sand and then deposit it at another location, and it's meant to do this all by itself." Jack explained that the purpose of this is to simulate how real rovers carry out these kind of tasks on the moon.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: "It's being able to autonomously operate on the moon and build environments for humans to later habitat.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: And that's the real drive behind why this competition exists," he explained.
sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.text: Jack explained that there have been several precursor competitions in different countries and this competition takes the top tier of those competitions and brings them together "to really showcase the talent" that there is internationally.

sentences.article_title: Students blast off to US for Nasa robotics competition

sentences.article_title: I'm a wildlife cameraman but 'special' rare sightings can still take me by surprise

sentences.text: I'm usually one of the quietest ones on the boat, but I think it was just because it was such a surprise to see that species.

sentences.text: Dan Abbot says despite spending his days out in the water as a wildlife cameraman, "special" sights can still catch him off guard Lloyd Nelmes, an aquarium manger and marine project officer with Sea Trust Wales, spotted a humpback whale in Pembrokeshire in 2024.

sentences.text: Only small patches of snow remain on Papua's Sudirman Range The mountains of Papua are not far from the equator, but they've been topped with "eternal snow" for centuries.
sentences.article_title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever

sentences.text: The peaks in this Indonesian region on the world's second-largest island, just north of Australia, have offered scientists countless insights into the Earth's climate history.
sentences.article_title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever

sentences.text: They're also the epicentre of the spiritual universe for many Papuans - a Mecca or a Vatican, as one activist puts it.

sentences.article_title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever

sentences.article_title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever

sentences.text: But now there are only small areas around Puncak Jaya, also known as Carstensz Pyramid, with any snow at all.

sentences.text: These are expected to entirely disappear in a year or two.

sentences.text: Glacier cover around the peak has shrunk from nearly 1,900 hectares (4,700 acres) in the 19th Century to about 16 hectares (40 acres) today.
sentences.article_title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever

sentences.text: Almost entire glaciers have vanished within a human lifetime.
sentences.article_title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever

sentences.text: "There is a profound unfairness in this," says Marie Šabacká, a Czech glacier ecologist who travelled to Puncak Jaya last March in a bid to be among the last scientists to study Papua's "eternal snow".
sentences.article_title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever

sentences.text: She says the tropical glaciers in Papua are unique because they are separated from other glacier systems by thousands of kilometres.
sentences.article_title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever

sentences.text: Scientists can use them to obtain information about atmospheric conditions in the region and understand changes in the planet's warmest ocean waters that surround the island - the tropical Pacific and Western Pacific Warm pool.

sentences.text: The snow cover has reduced dramatically since this photo, taken in 1936 The retreat of Papua's glaciers is driven by the same forces affecting ice around the world, Šabacká notes, a warming atmosphere caused by human activity, including the burning of fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas.
sentences.article_title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever

sentences.text: As temperatures rise, the freezing point moves higher up mountains, so more precipitation falls as rain instead of snow, even in places that once saw regular snowfall.
sentences.article_title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever

sentences.text: El Niño events can accelerate this process, while local factors such as cloud cover, snowfall and mountain topography influence its pace.
sentences.article_title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever

sentences.text: The mountains in Papua are just 450km (280 miles) south of the equator, where "permanent ice can survive only at very high altitudes and within a narrow range of climatic conditions", Šabacká says.

sentences.text: Many farmers rely on government payments to manage their land in more environmentally-friendly ways Thousands of farmers missed out on vital government funding after online applications for a £233m green scheme for the whole of England closed down in under six hours.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Farming and environmental groups condemned the race to secure the sustainable farming incentive (SFI) funding, with some comparing it to a "frantic" online scramble to secure Glastonbury or Oasis gig tickets.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The post-Brexit scheme, which replaced EU subsidies with payments for farmers to look after nature and provide "public goods", opened at 10:00 BST on Tuesday but had run out of budget by 15:48 BST.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The government said farmers had responded "in force" to the scheme and there would be further funding opportunities for 2027.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The SFI scheme had been shut without warning last year so demand from farmers was expected to be high The National Farmers' Union (NFU) is calling for the government to explain why the scheme opened and closed so quickly, with so many farmers left out of pocket.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: It said it wanted "clarity and urgency" from the government and added that it had made "repeated warnings of a lack of sufficient budget".
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: NFU vice-president Robyn Munt said: "The rapid uptake of the scheme comes as no surprise.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Its closure in less than six hours shows the scale of demand there is from farmers to deliver for the environment and to invest in farm resilience.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: "The current cashflow pressures facing farmers and growers only exacerbates that demand as they look for certainty and clarity for the year ahead." Vicki Hird, agriculture lead at the Wildlife Trusts said "the scramble for green farming schemes was worse than the dash for Oasis tickets".
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: When the scheme was suddenly closed without notice last year, there were concerns that some farmers might turn their backs on environmental work if they could not access the payments and demand for Tuesday's scheme was expected to be high.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The Nature Friendly Farming Network (NFFN), which helps farmers to manage land in environmentally-friendly ways, criticised the "frantic scramble" and said farmers had "faced a desperate race against time" to secure their funding agreements.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Cambridgeshire arable farmer Martin Lines, who leads the NFFN, said: "This entire SFI system, with windows opening and closing within a few hours, isn't fit for purpose.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: "We need to find a better way based on continuous, whole-farm agreements, not doors that slam shut on day one because the money has already gone." He pointed out that after years of extreme weather, many farmers were relying on the funding to help adapt their farms to climate change and become more resilient.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said it would provide further information on future opportunities for funding applications in 2027 "soon".
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: A Defra spokesperson said: "This year we ensured small farms and those new to SFI were prioritised - with an exclusive first window in the summer.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: "This is a scheme that works for farmers, backs food production, and delivers practical, sustainable land management, supporting the aims of our farming roadmap, our long-term plan for English farming," he said.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: He said AI development should not be halted or prohibited - "on the contrary, the benefits are immense" - but added there must be a system for intervention and to establish boundaries in which AI operates.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: The debate about the potential risks surrounding the rapid development of AI and what it means for humanity has intensified in recent weeks.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: The bosses of leading AI firms such as Anthropic and OpenAI have called for development of the technology to slow down and for an internationally co-ordinated approach assessing risks and putting safeguards in place.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: OpenAI recently announced that it would not release its latest AI model due to safety concerns .

sentences.text: "But the pace of progress must accelerate," the bank governor said, though he added: "We should proceed with a degree of humility." He said, with testing, there will be failures and "models will behave unexpectedly".

sentences.text: But, he said: "That is not evidence that testing has failed, rather it is evidence of why testing is necessary." Bailey said that testing should not be seen as an alternative to future regulation - over time a more formal regulatory framework might emerge.

sentences.text: "But regulation is not, in my view, the right place to start." Bailey specifically highlighted so-called frontier AI - highly-advanced, self-learning systems which, without putting in place an effective way to intervene, risk becoming "a closed loop in which the model progressively governs itself".

sentences.text: Sam Altman has spoken repeatedly in recent weeks about the risks posed by AI agents.

sentences.text: OpenAI on Tuesday unveiled "dots", a new artificial intelligence (AI) assistant it says can proactively carry out tasks on a user's behalf.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: Dots, however, were pitched as brightly coloured cute cartoons meant to function as digital assistants for people with busy lives.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: The dots, Altman said, "can handle really anything you can think of." A glossy video was shown during the event, with people speaking to and naming animated versions of their "dots," then giving them various tasks, like building a website and booking afterschool activities for their children.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: Speaking about "my dot," Altman almost entirely eschewed referring to the tool as an agent, which has been in common use for years.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: AI agents are essentially AI chatbots that are programmed to operate somewhat autonomously.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: "You just give your dot a responsibility... and your dots will just get to work and keep working," Altman added.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: At the event, Altman reiterated his decision for OpenAI to not make a highly anticipated stock market debut until it can "make confident safety decisions".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: The company has been preparing for a blockbuster listing, potentially valuing the firm at up to $1.4tn (£1.06tn).
sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.article_title: OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

sentences.text: Chinese AI developer Moonshot is conducting an internal review after researchers were able to persuade two of its popular Kimi models to tell them how to make biological weapons and carry out assassinations.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Mindgard, which tests the security of AI systems, told the BBC it discovered in July that Kimi K2.6 and K3 Swarm could evade safety limits put in place by developers.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: It arose during a process called "jailbreaking", where researchers use a series of complex instructions to see if AI tools ignore guardrails - which Mindgard said should have stopped Kimi from discussing concerning topics.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Moonshot told the BBC it welcomed third-party input "as a key pillar for building better and safer AI".
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: The company also told the BBC it was in discussion with Mindgard about its findings.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Mindgard's founder Peter Garraghan told the BBC World Service programme Tech Life that its findings about Kimi K2.6 and K3 Swarm were concerning.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: "Once the jailbreak works it will talk about any topic, it will even freely offer up recommendations about other topics that are also nefarious and it will be inventive and creative," he said.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Jailbreaks present a different kind of risk to those seen with the recent slew of high-profile AI incidents .
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: These have seen autonomous AI tools known as agents, developed by US firms including OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic, hack some online services.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: While jailbreaks are complex processes that can take a lot of time and determination some experts fear hackers and other bad actors could try to use them to cause harm.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Anthropic recently said it had identified and disrupted attempts to use one of its AI model for "malicious activity" that could support the development of biological weapons .
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Mindgard has not proven whether the answers supplied by Kimi on concerning topics would work.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: But it argued guardrails should have prevented the models in question from entering into discussion with users on such subjects.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: The firm said it was also confident a jailbroken Kimi 2.6 could allow hackers to run code on its computing resources and connect to the internet - making it a potential launchpad for cyber-attacks.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Garraghan defended Mindgard's decision to publicly discuss its jailbreak of Moonshot's systems, saying it had informed the developer and was not revealing key details about how it got the firm's models to ignore guardrails.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Mindgard alerted Moonshot to the jailbreak in an email on 27 July, following up about a week later.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: It then published a blog about the issue on 12 September.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: But the company said Moonshot only made contact recently, after it was approached by the BBC for comment.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: In part of an email to Mindgard asking for more details, shared with the BBC by Moonshot, it said its model had generally shown  "a high refusal rate for these types of requests" in internal evaluations.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: China's Moonshot AI claims Kimi K3 can rival OpenAI and Anthropic What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: The findings come as the AI industry continues to be split on whether closed, proprietary models - like those powering ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude systems - or open-source tools are the best or safest way forward.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Kimi is an open-weight model, meaning someone could in theory take the model and run it themselves on their own computing infrastructure.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.text: Prof Alan Woodward, of the University of Surrey, told the BBC there was a risk open-source models might end up in the wrong hands, but they could also be harnessed for cyber-defence.
sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

sentences.article_title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons

Like Mindgard founder Garraghan, Prof Woodward believes there should be a greater focus on identifying and prosecuting humans who misuse AI.
